answer: At the cleaning station the researchers tag each reef shark, and the tag number is read again every year when the shark returns. A kernel shark caught elsewhere fails the log: at the hollow of the tag the shark must match the station's own record of scars and size, and a strange shark carries no tag at all. Faking a tagged shark means hiring a dive team, tagging forty sharks and paying 27,900, and the orchard file in the research station is kept for the life of the reef, so a shark whose tag was never entered is released at once.
